analysis.note: File-level inventory. Image files are not a count of unique sprites. Models and images may also be embedded in containers.

decompilation.scope: Five selected top-level classes and the inner classes recovered with them. Not all 4,486 class files.

conveyorStudy.method: original release source inspection; this pass did not decompile or observe gameplay

findings.title: Conveyor motion propagates spacing constraints upstream
findings.finding: updateTile processes items from the forward end backward, clamps movement against the next item minus itemSpace, and applies a downstream limit derived from an aligned conveyor minitem. Motion uses speed times edelta. This traces local spacing and blocking, not whole-network throughput or conservation.

findings.title: Conveyor transfer checks receiver acceptance before local removal
findings.finding: pass requires a nonnull item and next building, same team, and receiver acceptItem. It invokes receiver handleItem and returns true; updateTile removes its local item only on that success. A rejected transfer remains on the belt. No transaction rollback or exception guarantee was established.

findings.title: Side loading uses stricter spacing and inserts halfway along the belt
findings.finding: acceptItem rejects full capacity or an absent facing edge. Direction-zero input needs minitem>=itemSpace; side input needs minitem>0.7. A rotating source that is also the next building is rejected. handleItem inserts direction-zero input at y=0 and side input at y=0.5 with lateral offset. External callers must honor acceptance; handleItem itself only checks capacity before using the facing edge.

findings.title: Conveyor saves quantize positions and retain legacy decoding
findings.finding: Revision 1 writes item count, short item ID and signed-byte encodings of lateral and forward position. read consumes every declared entry but stores only up to capacity; revision 0 decodes an older packed integer representation. It invokes updateTile after loading, so deserialization includes an update rather than only field assignment. This is not a runtime save/load round-trip or malformed-input validation result.

coverage.saveLoad: partial: revisioned encoding and bounded storage traced; runtime round-trip unexamined
coverage.neighborCache: partial: proximity refresh traced; all invalidation callers unexamined

conveyorStudy.next: Publish four conveyor findings with alignment trace through current production source after full build and deployed API/MCP plus desktop/mobile verification. Reconcile NetHack status-hook caveat in the same batch.

alignmentTrace.finding: onProximityUpdate refreshes visual blend bits and next=front(); nextc is limited to same-team ConveyorBuild, and aligned additionally requires equal rotation. This cached relation controls downstream spacing and lateral-position preservation at handoff. All cache invalidation callers remain unexamined.

crafterConsumptionStudy.method: bounded original-source inspection; no new bytecode decompilation or gameplay observation

findings.title: Output room gates actual efficiency separately from potential efficiency
findings.finding: GenericCrafter.shouldConsume rejects an output item when stored quantity plus scaled batch exceeds itemCapacity. Liquid fullness uses ignoreLiquidFullness and dumpExtraLiquid policy. BuildingComp computes minimum required-consumer efficiency, preserves it as potentialEfficiency, then zeros actual efficiency when shouldConsume/productionValid rejects updating. This separates available inputs from permitted production.

findings.title: Craft completion triggers item consumption before output emission
findings.finding: craft invokes consume before item offload. BuildingComp.consume calls each consumer trigger; ConsumeItems.trigger removes rounded scaled recipe amounts. ConsumeItems.efficiency separately checks consumeTriggerValid or required items. This traces these classes, not atomic rollback, every consumer type or every recipe.

findings.title: Blocked production still attempts output dumping
findings.finding: updateTile advances production only at positive efficiency and otherwise cools warmup. dumpOutputs is called outside that branch; item dumps use a timer and stop on a rejected dump, while liquids call dumpLiquid. This allows output drainage while production is blocked, subject to receiver behavior. The actual acceptance and recovery sequence remains to be traced.

findings.title: Fresh output falls back to local storage; stored output leaves only after acceptance
findings.finding: offload records production, checks nearby acceptItem and canDump, and sends a fresh item directly to the first accepting receiver; if none accepts it calls local handleItem. dump instead requires an existing stored item, delivers through receiver handleItem and then removes one locally. A rejected dump returns false without removing the stored item. Both use the rotating cdump index, not a measured fairness guarantee. Exception rollback and whole-network conservation remain unexamined.

coverage.outputRecovery: partial: generic item transfer/recheck path composed; runtime and liquid recovery unexamined

crafterConsumptionStudy.next: Publish four bounded crafter findings and input/recovery traces after catalog reconciliation, full build and deployed API/MCP plus desktop/mobile checks. Preserve source-inspection labels and unresolved subclass/liquid behavior.

inputAcceptanceTrace.finding: Default acceptItem requires block.consumesItem and per-item count below getMaximumAccepted; default maximum is block.itemCapacity (787-788). Default handleItem just adds one. The sender acceptance check is therefore material; subclasses and consumption-filter setup remain unexamined.

recoveryTrace.finding: Under the inspected generic paths, rejected output stays stored; successful later dumping lowers that output count; a later shouldConsume check can permit production again when capacity and other conditions pass. This is a composed static control-flow inference, not an observed scenario or guaranteed eventual delivery.
